entities.title: The Worker's tests
entities.summary: npm test runs the real handler in Node against a fake GitHub.
criteria: The page is served at / and /index.html, and anything else is 404.
Without the three secrets, /auth/me says so and nobody can start a sign-in.
A sign-in goes to GitHub with PKCE and a state bound to the browser, and asks for repo only when chosen.
A good callback sets a sealed, HttpOnly session without the token in it, and returns to the page.
A wrong state, no pending cookie, a refused code, a forged, damaged or expired cookie sign nobody in.
The door needs a session, reads only, keeps to its allowlist and adds the token itself.
Sign-out works only from the app's own origin.
The return path stays on the app's host.

checks.symbol: without OAuth settings it says so and signs nobody in
sign-in goes to GitHub with PKCE and a state bound to the browser
private repositories are asked for only when chosen
the callback opens a sealed, HttpOnly session and returns to the page
a callback with the wrong state, or no cookie, signs nobody in
a refused code signs nobody in
cookies sealed with another secret, or damaged, are not sessions
the proxy needs a session, reads only, and adds the token itself
sign-out only from the page's own origin
the return path stays on the app's host

entities.details: The workflow runs the same tests on every pull request and before every deploy ([pipeline](.github/.dev/pipeline.json)). Nothing tests the callback's 503, the 401 that clears a session, or the page's use of these routes.
